choices.content: \(a\gt9,\) but we can put no bounds on \(b\)

question.prompt: Five times \(A\)’s money added to \(B\)’s money is more than \(\$51.00.\) Three times \(A\)’s money minus \(B\)’s money is \(\$21.00.\) If \(a\) represents \(A\)’s money in dollars and \(b\) represents \(B\)’s money in dollars, then:

solutions.explanation:
The two statements translate to
\[
5a+b>51,
\qquad 3a-b=21.
\]
The opposite signs of \(b\) suggest adding the relations to eliminate it. Since the second expression equals \(21\), this gives
\[
(5a+b)+(3a-b)>51+21,
\]
so \(8a>72\) and therefore \(a>9\). The equation then gives
\[
b=3a-21>3\cdot9-21=6.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{a>9\text{ and }b>6}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Eliminate B's money
